subject: Limitations & Refunds: LoL cap, refund mechanics for prepaid terminations
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme MSA redline + question on refunds and caps

Hi Karthik,

Please find attached our redline to the MSA and the Order Form (OrderForm_v3). A few of our counsel's high-level flags we want to get aligned on before we proceed:

- Limitation of Liability (Section 9): Counsel is concerned the proposed cap is unclear when combined with termination-for-convenience and prepaid fees. They want language confirming that the cap does not limit liability for certain carve-outs (willful misconduct, IP infringement, and indemnities) — standard.
- Prepaid fees on termination: We pay a significant portion of the first year upfront. The current draft doesn't say whether Acme is entitled to a pro-rata refund if Redwood terminates for convenience or fails to deliver certain services. Our default position is a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees plus reasonable wind-down assistance.
- Wind-down assistance: Counsel wants explicit carve-out from the cap for reasonable transition/wind-down assistance and related costs.

Can you confirm Redwood's commercial position on: (1) whether the LoL cap will exclude wind-down assistance and refunds; (2) whether refunds are pro-rata for unused prepaid services on termination; and (3) timing/format for returning prepaid amounts?

We're trying to avoid looping too late into legal review cycles — if you can share Redwood's proposed counter-language (highlighting carve-outs and refund mechanics) we'll get that to our counsel for a clean redline round.

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Redline_20260223.pdf, OrderForm_v3_trackchanges.docx

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme MSA redline + question on refunds and caps

Marissa / Nikhil — forwarding Acme's redline and three asks (cap carve-outs, prepaid refund treatment, wind-down assistance).

Quick take: commercial team should offer a pragmatic compromise that protects Redwood economics while preserving enterprise comfort. Key constraints from our side:
- We cannot agree to uncapped refunds identical to indemnities — refunds must be quantifiable and limited.
- Wind-down assistance creates cost spikes (people + GPU time). We prefer to exclude reasonable transition assistance from the cap but with a commercial cap (e.g., not unlimited).
- For prepaid fees: standard approach is a pro-rata refund of unused services upon termination for convenience, subject to a notice window and deductions for services already delivered. For termination-for-cause (customer breach) typically no refund.

Ask legal (cc'd): can you draft 2 short options we can present:
1) Customer-friendly: carve-out for refunds and wind-down assistance from LoL; pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refundable amount = prepaid remaining term - delivered value) with a 30-day notice offset and capped wind-down assistance equal to 3 months of MRR.
2) Provider-friendly: LoL cap is overall with explicit carve-outs only for indemnities/willful misconduct; prepaid fees non-refundable except for specific service failures; wind-down assistance paid but included in cap.

Marissa — if you want to propose a middle-ground commercial fallback now (before legal redline) that we'd pitch to Acme, that will speed things up.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme MSA redline + question on refunds and caps

On Tue, Feb 24, 2026 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Nikhil — forwarding Acme's redline and three asks (cap carve-outs, prepaid refund treatment, wind-down assistance).
> 
> Quick take: commercial team should offer a pragmatic compromise...

Dropping in proposed language and commercial fallback we can present to Acme this afternoon. Legal — feel free to redline. I tried to keep things tight and executable.

Proposed commercial compromise (single paragraph for MSA + mirrored in Order Form):
- Limitation of Liability: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Redwood arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) USD 1,000,000. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitation of liability shall not apply to (i) liabilities arising from Redwood's indemnification obligations, (ii) liability arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (iii) Customer payments or refunds owed under Section X (Termination; Refunds) and reasonable wind-down and transition assistance fees expressly agreed in writing by the parties."

- Refund mechanics (Section X): "If Redwood terminates an Order Form for convenience, Customer will be entitled to a pro-rata refund of prepaid, unused fees for the remainder of the then-current prepaid period, calculated on a daily basis, less any amounts due for services already rendered. Refunds will be processed within sixty (60) days following termination, provided Customer returns any Redwood property and complies with transition cooperation obligations. Refunds do not apply in the event of Customer termination for cause resulting from Customer breach."

- Wind-down assistance (SOW/Order Form addendum): "Reasonable transition and wind-down assistance (including handover of models, export of data, and limited operational support) will be provided for a fee; such fees shall be excluded from the limitation of liability up to a cap equal to three (3) months of the then-current monthly committed spend under the applicable Order Form unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Commercial rationale: this preserves customer comfort (explicit carve-out for refunds and transition) while bounding Redwood's exposure (12-months or $1M cap, wind-down carve-out capped). It also gives a clear refund timing and process.

If legal is happy with the wording, we should return a clean redline to Acme that inserts the above into the MSA and a short clause into Order Form. If Acme pushes back on the wind-down cap, consider swapping to "reasonable and documented" vs hard numeric cap as a fallback.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Limitations & Refunds: LoL cap, refund mechanics for prepaid terminations

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the quick commercial proposal. A few quick notes from our side and counsel: 

- The cap formula (greater of 12-months fees or $1M) is workable. Counsel asks that the cap floor be expressed as "fees paid or payable" to avoid disputes for prepay timing — we'll clean that up in their redline.
- We appreciate carving out indemnities and willful misconduct. Please confirm explicitly that refunds and reasonable transition/wind-down assistance are carved out from the cap (your text does, but counsel wants the same in a single cross-reference sentence).
- On refund timing: 60 days is acceptable. For the calculation, counsel prefers "unused prepaid days on a daily basis" as you suggested.

Next steps: please have Redwood legal send a clean redline of the MSA + Order Form with the proposed clauses and call out the wind-down cap (3 months of committed spend) as negotiable. If you can get that to us by end of day tomorrow we'll move this to counsel review and aim to get back within 48-72 hours.

Sarah Li
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
